title: zazzle command features
description: The behavior the commands offer beyond answering: bounded output, checked edits, reading one symbol, the terse C# view, C# structure from the indexer and cleaning piped output.

entities.name: Capped, ranked output
entities.description: Every answer is bounded and says how to get more.
entities.behavior: find shows at most 50 matching lines (-m), grouped by file, ordinary files before tests and shallower before deeper, each line clipped to 240 bytes around the match; -l and -c list at most 200 files. ls shows at most 150 entries to depth 2, outline 200 symbols to depth 3, refs 50 uses and 20 definitions. read keeps the head and tail of each file (or terse view) within about 3000 tokens and names the elided range to read next; --full lifts that. clean keeps the head and tail within its own budget (default 8000) and says how much was cut. Any other successful answer is cut at a line boundary at about 8000 tokens (--budget). Each cap ends in a footer that says how to narrow or continue.
entities.outcome: An agent gets a bounded answer and the next command to run, instead of a flood that fills its context.
constraints: Tokens are estimated from bytes, about 3.5 bytes per token (tokens.rs from_bytes).
read's budget applies to each file named; read and clean output is not cut by the global budget.
Errors, edit results, status, help and version are never cut.

entities.name: Checked, confined, atomic edits
entities.description: An edit lands only on the file version the caller read, only inside its working directory, and all at once.
entities.behavior: edit replaces text that must be unique unless --all is given, replaces or deletes a line range, inserts after a line, or creates a new file. Every edit except --create needs proof the caller read the current code: --expect with at least the first four hex digits of the sha `read --source` showed, or, for a line range, --at anchors from `read --source --anchors` that still match. A refusal says to read again with --source and never reveals the current sha or anchors. Just before writing, the file is hashed again and the edit refused if it changed. The new content is written to a temporary file beside it and renamed over it, with its permissions; new text follows the file's line-ending style. Edits in one daemon are serialised. The answer names the lines changed and the new sha, which the caller may use for its next edit.
entities.outcome: An agent cannot overwrite changes it has not seen, edit code it only saw as a terse view, write outside the directory it was started in, or leave a half-written file.
constraints: Paths are resolved through symlinks and must lie inside the working directory.
Binary files are refused.
A file with several hard links is rewritten in place, not by rename.
Extended attributes are not carried over by the rename.
--create refuses an existing file.
Text given on standard input (--new -) must be UTF-8.

entities.name: Read one symbol
entities.description: `read FILE --symbol NAME` shows one symbol with the doc comments, comments and attributes directly above it.
entities.behavior: The outline gives the symbol's range, which is extended upward over the lines directly above it that start like a comment, attribute or decorator for the file's language (`///`, `/* */`, `#[...]`, C# `[...]`, `@decorator`, Python `#`). NAME is the symbol's name or the last parts of its qualified name (`Invoice.Total`, `billing::tax::total`), with containers taken from nesting; `impl Trait for Type` counts as the type and generics are ignored. Exact case is tried first, then any case. Overloads are picked by parameter types, `Total(decimal, int)` or `Total()`: types are compared as written in the declaration with spaces ignored, `Type name` and `name: Type` declarations both work, defaults, attributes and modifiers are ignored, receivers (`self`, `&self`, Python's `self`/`cls`) are not counted, and an untyped parameter matches by name; a list that fits no overload lists the ones there are. Several matches are listed, numbered, with their lines, kind, qualified name and declaration line, and the parameter types or `#N` pick one; no match lists names that contain it, or points at `zazzle outline`. The header names the symbol, and the usual read budget applies; on a C# file the range is shown in the terse view unless --source.
entities.outcome: An agent reads exactly the function or type it needs, with its documentation, without first finding its line range.
constraints: --symbol cannot be combined with PATH:A-B, --around, --head or --tail.
At most 10 candidates are listed.
Symbols are only as good as the outline: syntax trees for Rust, Python, C, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript and TSX up to 1 MiB, line heuristics otherwise.
Parameter types are compared as text: `decimal` does not match `System.Decimal`.

entities.name: Terse C# view
entities.description: `read FILE.cs` returns zazzle-csharp-indexer's terse behavioural view of the file instead of its code, with source line numbers and no sha.
entities.behavior: For a .cs file read without --source or --anchors, the daemon asks the indexer's `view` tool for the file (relative to the git work tree that holds it) and shows its lines for the requested range: `N` unchanged, `N~` changed, `A-B ⋯ note` hidden, under a header naming the shortening steps and saying `read --source for the code and its sha`. Ranges, --symbol and the budget work on the view. When there is no view (no indexer, not in a git work tree, an indexer error), the source is returned with a line saying why.
entities.outcome: An agent understands C# code from fewer tokens, and still has to read the real code before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
The file must be inside a git work tree.
The indexer is found as $ZAZZLE_INDEXER, else beside zazzled, else on PATH; its daemon is started when nothing listens and may take several seconds the first time.

entities.name: Terse HTML and Razor view
entities.description: `read` on an .html, .htm, .xhtml, .cshtml or .razor file returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the markup, with source line numbers and no sha.
entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, markup.rs hides comments of three or more lines, <style> and <svg> elements alone on their lines, runs of two or more <meta>/<link>/<base> lines and, in Razor, runs of @using/@addTagHelper/@removeTagHelper lines; it shortens class values with more than 4 classes to the first 3 and style values over 40 characters. <script>, <pre>, <textarea> and Razor @code, @functions and @{ } blocks are shown as they are. read renders the result like the C# view: `N`, `N~`, `A-B ⋯ note` under a header naming the steps and --source. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads pages and Razor views without paying for styles, drawings, boilerplate and utility-class lists, and still has to read the real markup before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
The rules are line-based: a comment or element sharing its first or last line with other markup is not hidden.
C# in Razor @code and @functions blocks is shortened only when zazzle-csharp-indexer runs and the file is in a git work tree; @{ } blocks stay as they are.

entities.name: Terse CSS, SCSS, Sass and Less view
entities.description: `read` on a .css, .scss, .sass or .less file returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the stylesheet, with source line numbers and no sha.

sources.symbol: CSS, SCSS, Sass and Less terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, styles.rs hides comments of four or more lines (and SCSS // runs), source map comments, runs of two or more @import/@use/@forward lines, @font-face and @keyframes blocks (as one note with the font family or animation name), vendor-prefixed declarations whose block also sets the plain property, and SCSS and Sass @debug lines (Less is read like SCSS; indented Sass finds blocks by indentation); it shortens url(data:…) values longer than 60 characters. read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads stylesheets without paying for licence banners, font and animation boilerplate, duplicate prefixes and inline images, and still has to read the real stylesheet before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
The rules are line-based: a comment or block sharing its first or last line with other rules is not hidden, and minified files gain little.
Comments of three lines or fewer stay, since they are usually section titles.

entities.name: Terse JSON, YAML and TOML view
entities.description: `read` on a .json, .jsonc, .json5, .yaml, .yml or .toml file, or a known lock file (Cargo.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock, pdm.lock, composer.lock, Pipfile.lock), returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the file, with source line numbers and no sha.

sources.symbol: JSON, YAML, TOML and Markdown terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, data.rs keeps the first and last of a run of 10+ sibling list items (JSON array values, YAML `- ` items, TOML array values; items spanning lines only when they all name the same keys) and collapses the rest; in lock files it does the same for any 10+ sibling entries. It collapses runs of 6+ TOML [[tables]] with the same name to their first and last, `#` comment blocks (JSON `//`) of 4+ lines, and YAML block scalars and TOML multi-line strings of 6+ lines after their opening line, and cuts quoted strings over 120 characters to their first 40. read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads configuration, data and lock files without paying for long arrays, repeated tables and embedded blobs, and still has to read the real file before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
The rules are line-based: minified JSON on one line comes back as source.
Multi-line list items collapse only when they name the same keys, so lists of different things, such as CI steps, stay.

entities.name: Terse Markdown view
entities.description: `read` on a .md, .markdown or .mdx file returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the file, with source line numbers and no sha.

sources.symbol: JSON, YAML, TOML and Markdown terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, md.rs hides HTML comments (multi-line ones as one note), lines made only of badge images, runs of 2+ link reference definitions and lists of 3+ entries that only link to anchors, and leaves fenced code and front matter alone. read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads READMEs and changelogs without paying for badges, link tables and tables of contents, and still has to read the real file before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
Only images with badge-like sources count as badges; other images stay.

entities.name: Terse XML view
entities.description: `read` on an XML file (.xml, project and MSBuild files, XAML, plists, resources, schemas, .nuspec, .manifest) returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the file, with source line numbers and no sha.

sources.symbol: XML, INI and Dockerfile terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, xml.rs collapses comments of three or more lines and runs of ten or more sibling elements with the same tag (each on one line or closing at its own indentation) to their first and last, and cuts quoted values over 120 characters and runs of 120+ base64-style characters to their first 40. read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads project files, resource files and XML data without paying for long reference lists, repeated records and embedded blobs, and still has to read the real file before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
The rules are line-based: elements sharing lines, or minified XML, are not collapsed.

entities.name: Terse INI and Dockerfile view
entities.description: `read` on an INI-style file (.ini, .cfg, .properties, .editorconfig) or a Dockerfile (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, *.dockerfile, Containerfile) returns a terse view built in zazzled instead of the file, with source line numbers and no sha.

sources.symbol: XML, INI and Dockerfile terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, config.rs collapses comment blocks of four or more lines (`;` and `#` in INI files, `#` in Dockerfiles except `# syntax=` and `# escape=` directives), runs of three or more Dockerfile LABEL lines, and six or more package names one per continued line after a RUN line, and cuts runs of 120+ base64-style characters. read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent reads configuration files and Dockerfiles without paying for long comment banners, label blocks and package lists, and still has to read the real file before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
Explanatory comment blocks of four or more lines are hidden like banners; shorter ones stay.

entities.name: Terse Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Rust, Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift, C, C++, Ruby, PHP, Scala, Perl, Lua, Elixir, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Clojure, Erlang, R, Julia, Zig, Objective-C, Groovy, PowerShell, SQL, Visual Basic, Fortran, Pascal, COBOL, Nim and shell view
entities.description: `read` on a .py, .pyi, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .mts, .cts, .tsx, .dart, .rs, .go, .java, .kt, .kts, .swift, .c, .h, .cpp, .cc, .cxx, .hpp, .hh, .hxx, .rb, .rake, .php, .scala, .sc, .pl, .pm, .lua, .ex, .exs, .hs, .ml, .fs, .fsx, .clj, .cljs, .cljc, .erl, .hrl, .r, .jl, .zig, .m, .groovy, .gvy, .gradle, .ps1, .psm1, .sql, .vb, .f, .f90 (and other Fortran extensions), .pas, .dpr, .lpr, .dpk, .cbl, .cob, .cpy, .nim, .nims, .sh, .bash, .zsh or .ksh file returns a terse view built in zazzled with tree-sitter instead of the code, with source line numbers and no sha. Nim, SQL and COBOL files get line-based views from nim.rs, sql.rs and cobol.rs.

sources.symbol: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Rust, Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift, C, C++, Ruby, PHP, Scala, Perl, Lua, Elixir, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Clojure, Erlang, R, Julia, Zig, Objective-C, Groovy, PowerShell, SQL, Visual Basic, Fortran, Pascal, COBOL, Nim and shell terse view

entities.behavior: Without --source or --anchors, terse.rs parses the file and hides runs of top-level imports spanning two or more lines, logging statements alone on their lines with no assignment, await, yield, increment or decrement in their arguments, region marker comments, multi-line constructors that only store parameters (shown as one note with the parameter list) catch clauses that only log and rethrow the caught exception, Go `if err != nil` blocks that only log and return the error (kept on one line), and `if` blocks that only check a log level and log; it drops public, private and protected from TypeScript class members and Java declarations, and Rust pub except on pub use, and gives locals of 6+ characters the C# view's short names at their declaration and every use (locals.rs). read renders the result like the C# view. A file with nothing to shorten, or over 1 MiB, is returned as source with its sha.
entities.outcome: An agent understands Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Rust, Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift, C, C++, Ruby, PHP, Scala, Perl, Lua, Elixir, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Clojure, Erlang, R, Julia, Zig, Objective-C, Groovy, PowerShell, SQL, Visual Basic, Fortran, Pascal, COBOL, Nim and shell code from fewer tokens, and still has to read the real code before it can edit it.
constraints: The view carries no sha, so it cannot be used for --expect.
Rules are syntactic: a logger is recognised by its name, and `print` is never hidden.
A local is renamed only where every place its name appears in its function can be renamed safely; otherwise it keeps its name.
Go log.Fatal and log.Panic calls are never hidden, since they stop the program.
A function whose parse has errors, or a C function a macro made the parser misread, keeps all its local names.
Shell scripts get no short locals: their variables are dynamically scoped and reached by bare name.
In Lua and Perl a name used inside its own declaration (`local x = x + 1`) means the outer variable, so that local keeps its name; Elixir rebinding renames every binding in the function together.
In Haskell, OCaml, F#, Clojure, Erlang, R and Julia a log call that is its block's last expression is the block's value and stays; Clojure log calls are hidden only in body forms.

Short locals apply to Zig, Objective-C and Groovy among the languages added with Haskell; Groovy only in methods without closures, lambdas or command calls, which its grammar misreads. The other added languages keep their names.
A SQL INSERT keeps its first and last rows; only 6+ rows each on its own line collapse.

entities.name: C# structure from the indexer
entities.description: overview, find-symbol, changed-since, git-log, git-blame and report-gap (zazzle_overview ... zazzle_report_gap) are answered by zazzle-csharp-indexer's daemon, which zazzle reaches as it does for the terse view; the indexer offers agents no tools of its own.
entities.behavior: zazzled finds the git work tree that holds the working directory, makes path arguments relative to it (refusing paths outside it), calls the indexer's tool of the same name over the daemon socket with the work tree as the session's root, starting the daemon when nothing listens, and rewrites the `root:path` references at the start of the answer's lines (or after an `A `, `M ` or `D ` mark) as paths relative to the working directory. The answer then goes through the same budget and session dedupe as every command; report-gap's is never deduplicated.
entities.outcome: An agent asks one server for files and for structure, and can read what find-symbol or changed-since names with zazzle read straight away.
constraints: The working directory must be inside a git work tree, and the indexer installed ($ZAZZLE_INDEXER, beside zazzled, or on PATH).
Answers wait up to 45 s for the indexer, which itself waits up to 30 s for a cold index before overview and find-symbol answer.
Paths with a colon in them are cut at the colon when rewritten.
The indexer's tools see only the one work tree zazzle attached, so their root filters are not offered.

entities.name: Clean piped output
entities.description: `CMD | zazzle clean` prints what an agent needs from a command's output, with every removal marked.
entities.behavior: clean reads standard input (up to 64 MiB) and runs its steps: terminal escapes removed, carriage-return redraws reduced to their last frame, trailing whitespace trimmed and blank runs squeezed; a JSON document or JSON Lines minified outside strings; grep, git grep or rg output regrouped by file in find's layout when every line parses and that is shorter; runs of identical lines collapsed with a count. Unless --lossless, the lossy steps also run: progress-bar runs reduced to their last line, base64 or hex runs of 200+ characters replaced by their length, and (not for JSON) lines over 600 bytes cut to 300. Last, the head and tail are kept within --budget. --as skips detection, --stats adds the steps and the token estimates before and after. The answer is stored with its input for an hour under an `[r:ID]`, and says `read-again r:ID --full` when the input was cut or a lossy step or the budget removed something (see the stored-outputs feature in macos/rust/zazzled/src). The same steps clean `zazzle run` output and the MCP proxy's texts.
entities.outcome: An agent can pipe any noisy output through one command and get a shorter text that still says what was removed.
constraints: If the cleaned text would be longer than the input, the input is passed through.
clean is not an MCP tool.
A clean answer gets no session id and is never deduplicated; without an output store (no HOME and no ZAZZLE_OUTPUTS_DIR) it carries no id at all.

entities.name: Language modules downloaded on demand
entities.description: Every tree-sitter grammar zazzled uses (34) ships as a shared library beside the zazzle download instead of inside zazzled; zazzled downloads one the first time a file needs it (or on `zazzle languages fetch`), accepts it only if its SHA-256 matches the manifest compiled into zazzled, and loads it.
entities.behavior: terse.rs and outline.rs ask modules.rs for every grammar. With JIT on (the default) a missing module downloads from icelander.net/downloads/zazzle/vX.Y.Z/languages/PLATFORM/, its SHA-256 is checked against the embedded manifest, it is stored in ~/.zazzle/v1/languages and opened with dlopen after checking its module format and tree-sitter ABI; with JIT off, or when the download fails, the file reads as source. `zazzle languages jit on|off` sets JIT, `zazzle languages fetch [NAME..]` downloads the missing modules, `zazzle languages` lists them. Outlines fall back to the line-based outline while a module is missing.
entities.outcome: zazzled stays small (6.8 MB instead of 82.4 MB) and a machine only holds the grammars of the languages it reads, while every module it runs is exactly one the release built.
constraints: A module is accepted only with the SHA-256 compiled into this zazzled, so modules belong to one release.
A development build without a manifest has no grammars: outlines are line-based and tree-sitter terse views are off.
A failed load is retried after a minute, or at once after `languages fetch` or `languages jit`.

The MCP proxy, which applies clean's steps to another server's results.
`zazzle run`, which applies a profile and then clean's steps to a command's output.

The change cursors zazzle_changed_since hands out.
